**Likely function:** This 496-aa protein is a **MurE ligase** (UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamate—meso-2,6-diaminopimelate ligase; **EC 6.3.2.13**), an enzyme in bacterial peptidoglycan precursor biosynthesis.

**Reaction:**

\[
\text{UDP-N-acetyl-}\alpha\text{-D-muramoyl-L-alanyl-D-glutamate}
+ \text{meso-2,6-diaminopimelate}
+ \text{ATP}
\rightarrow
\text{UDP-N-acetyl-}\alpha\text{-D-muramoyl-L-alanyl-}\gamma\text{-D-glutamyl-meso-2,6-diaminopimelate}
+ \text{ADP} + \text{phosphate} + \text{H}^+
\]

Thus, MurE uses ATP to ligate meso-diaminopimelate onto the UDP-linked peptidoglycan precursor.
